name: PuppyGraph
tagline: Zero-ETL graph query engine that runs Cypher and Gremlin directly on your lakehouse and SQL tables.
description: PuppyGraph is a graph query engine rather than a graph store: you map existing tables in Iceberg, Delta Lake, Hudi, Postgres, Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift, DuckDB and others to a graph schema, and it answers openCypher and Gremlin queries against them in place, with no data copy. A distributed, vectorized execution engine targets multi-hop queries over very large tables. It fits organizations that want graph analytics over data already in a lakehouse or warehouse without running ETL into a separate graph database. It is read-only, and latency depends on the underlying sources.

pricing.notes: Developer Edition is free (single node, two data sources); Enterprise is priced on CPU and memory, not data volume.

scale.notes: Enterprise runs multi-node clusters; storage scale is that of the underlying lakehouse or warehouse.

strengths: No ETL: queries graph structure directly over Iceberg, Delta, Postgres, Snowflake and more
One copy of data avoids sync drift between warehouse and graph database
Speaks both openCypher and Gremlin, so standard drivers and tools work
Pricing is by compute, not stored data volume
weaknesses: Read-only engine; writes go through the source systems
Latency depends on the source table formats and partitioning
Closed source and young product with frequent breaking changes in 0.x/1.x
